from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Objects cast shadows, revealing their shape.",
            "3D objects project onto 2D planes.",
            "Rotation changes the 2D shadow profile.",
            "Shadows help us infer 3D structure.",
            "This is the key to dimensional puzzles."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Concept of Projections", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Create a 3D cube
        cube = Cube(side_length=1.5, fill_opacity=0.5, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(cube, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(cube), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Project a shadow of the cube onto a 2D plane
        projection_plane = Polygon(
            np.array([-1, -1, 0]), np.array([1, -1, 0]), 
            np.array([1, 1, 0]), np.array([-1, 1, 0]),
            color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=0.3
        )
        self.place_at_grid(projection_plane, 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)
        shadow = Rectangle(width=1.2, height=1.2, color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(shadow, 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(projection_plane), FadeIn(shadow), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Rotate the cube to show changing shadow dimensions
        self.play(Rotate(cube, angle=PI/4, axis=OUT), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        # Update shadow (scale it to simulate projection change)
        self.play(shadow.animate.scale(1.2), run_time=1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Geometry of Flattening: Cross-Sections", [
            "Slicing a 3D object reveals interior structure.",
            "A sphere becomes a circle when sliced.",
            "Slices change as they pass through.",
            "We can infer volume from 2D slices.",
            "Interior geometry is hidden in plain sight."
        ])

        # Objects
        sphere = Sphere(radius=1.5, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        plane = Square(side_length=4, fill_opacity=0.5, color="#FF00FF")
        plane.rotate(PI/2, axis=RIGHT)
        
        # Cross section circle
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.8)
        
        self.place_at_grid(sphere, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(plane, 'C3')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        # Animate plane movement
        self.play(
            FadeIn(plane),
            plane.animate.shift(UP * 2)
        )
        self.add(circle)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, 'C3')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        # Slicing movement
        plane_tracker = ValueTracker(2)
        circle_tracker = ValueTracker(1.5)
        
        circle.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_width(2 * np.sqrt(max(0, 1.5**2 - plane_tracker.get_value()**2))))
        
        self.play(
            plane.animate.shift(DOWN * 4),
            plane_tracker.animate.set_value(-2),
            run_time=3
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF6600"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Folding and Unfolding: Net Geometry", ["3D surfaces can be unfolded into nets.", "Folding creates a 3D solid structure.", "Nets show how edges connect together."])
        
        # Cube net
        cube = Cube(side_length=1.5, fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_color=WHITE)
        net = VGroup(
            Square(side_length=1.5),
            Square(side_length=1.5).next_to(Square(side_length=1.5), UP, buff=0),
            Square(side_length=1.5).next_to(Square(side_length=1.5), DOWN, buff=0),
            Square(side_length=1.5).next_to(Square(side_length=1.5), LEFT, buff=0),
            Square(side_length=1.5).next_to(Square(side_length=1.5), RIGHT, buff=0),
        ).arrange_in_grid(2, 3, buff=0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(net, "C3", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(net))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Animate folding (simplified)
        self.play(Transform(net, self.place_at_grid(cube, "C3", scale_factor=0.6)))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        cube.set_stroke(color="#00FFFF", width=4)
        self.play(ShowPassingFlash(cube.copy().set_stroke(width=6), run_time=2))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Dimensional Shift Puzzle", [
            "Align 2D shapes to solve puzzles.",
            "Create 3D silhouettes to open locks.",
            "Dimensional shifts unlock new possibilities."
        ])

        # Animation objects
        square = Square(color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        cube = Cube(fill_color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.7, stroke_width=2)
        
        # Initial state
        self.place_at_grid(square, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(Create(square))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(Transform(square, self.place_at_grid(cube, 'C3', scale_factor=0.8)))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        shape_shift = VGroup(cube.copy())
        self.place_at_grid(shape_shift, 'C3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(shape_shift.animate.set_color("#00FF00").scale(1.2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")
        final_obj = cube.copy().set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(final_obj, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Rotate(final_obj, angle=PI/2, axis=UP))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Exploring Dimensional Shifts: From Flatland to 3D Geometry Puzzles
outline.target_audience: High school students interested in geometry and spatial reasoning

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Projections (1 Minute)
sections.content: Establish the foundation of dimensional interaction by demonstrating how lower-dimensional objects represent higher-dimensional ones. Use the 'Shadow Rule': a 3D object projects a 2D shadow. Understanding this inversion is key to solving dimensional shift puzzles.
sections.example: Visualizing a rotating 3D wireframe cube casting a changing 2D shadow on a wall, showing how the 'area' of the shadow fluctuates based on the orientation of the 3D object.

sections.title: The Geometry of Flattening: Cross-Sections (1.5 Minutes)
sections.content: Introduce how 3D shapes intersect with 2D planes. Explain that a 'slice' of a 3D object reveals its interior structure. This is the primary mechanic for puzzles where players must reconstruct a 3D object from 2D slices.
sections.example: A 'Sphere-Slicer' animation: As a plane passes through a sphere, the 2D cross-section transforms from a growing circle to a shrinking point, teaching students to infer volume from 2D data.

sections.title: Folding and Unfolding: Net Geometry (1.5 Minutes)
sections.content: Focus on the reversibility of dimensions. Explain 'Nets'—the 2D representation of a 3D solid's surface area. Crucial for understanding how to manipulate 3D shapes by 'unfolding' them onto a plane.
sections.example: The 'Dragon Origami' puzzle: A 3D dragon is flattened into a 2D pattern on a table. Students must identify which edges will connect when the 2D net is folded back into a 3D structure.

sections.title: Application: The Dimensional Shift Puzzle (1 Minute)
sections.content: Synthesize the knowledge. Present a challenge where a character is trapped in a 2D world and must escape by aligning 2D puzzles into a 3D configuration.
sections.example: A robot character (Bolt) is stuck in a 2D plane. To open a door, Bolt must rotate a 2D 'key' shape so that its projection onto the 'dimensional gate' creates a 3D silhouette that fits the lock's shape.
